conflicts.point: Whether physical supply chain tracking of advanced lithography equipment can effectively prevent unauthorized frontier model training without crippling open-source research and medical development.

positions.stance: Physical oversight anchored to ASML lithography equipment provides a verifiable and inspectable chokepoint that prevents unaligned scaling without harming essential innovation.
Hardware-level tracking starves open-source research and emerging economies while failing to stop distributed training on commodity hardware or algorithmic efficiency gains.

conflicts.point: Whether the existential risks of unmonitored frontier scaling outweigh the economic and medical costs of regulatory delays and market centralization.

positions.stance: Catastrophic civilizational control failure represents a permanent cost that justifies accepting domestic innovation flight and regulatory overhead as manageable externalities.
Enforcement bureaucracy and regulatory cartels inflict immediate, documented harms on labor and medical research to manage speculative future risks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether physical supply chain tracking of advanced lithography equipment can effectively prevent unauthorized frontier model training without crippling open-source research and medical development.
verdicts.rationale: Safety advocates provide concrete implementation mechanisms by anchoring oversight to physical lithography equipment managed through the Wassenaar Arrangement framework. Accelerationist claims regarding distributed training on commodity hardware remain speculative for the 2028 timeline without citing specific cluster architectures or interconnect bandwidths. Regulators can inspect physical manufacturing nodes far more reliably than they can audit decentralized code repositories.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Demonstrated scaling of frontier neural networks across distributed commodity chips connected by high-latency public internet lines would validate the accelerationist critique.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the existential risks of unmonitored frontier scaling outweigh the economic and medical costs of regulatory delays and market centralization.
verdicts.rationale: This conflict trades off between incommensurable values rather than factual errors. Safety advocates prioritize tail-risk civilizational survival, which discounts near-term market inefficiencies as manageable externalities. Skeptics focus on immediate, measurable harms to open-source research and labor markets caused by regulatory concentration. Neither framework provides an objective metric to weigh permanent extinction risk against present economic stagnation.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical calibration of unrecoverable control failure probabilities would allow policymakers to weigh tail-risk costs against documented economic harms.
